Hi Cody,

Glad both Thor P2s arrived and that one is running perfectly. Here's my take on the second one.

Normal mode is the setting the Thor P2 is built for. 
This unit is rated at 10 TH/s. Running it above that, including any turbo or boost mode, is overclocking: it runs hotter, needs good airflow, and voids the warranty.
 If that unit runs clean in normal mode and only complains when you push it past that, it's working within spec. Please keep it in normal mode for now. Even a small bump counts as overclocking, and I don't want a test run to cost you the warranty.

I looked for what the "vbus warning" and "powerboard warning" mean on the Thor P2 and couldn't find any documentation for them. I'm not going to guess. I've sent your case to JD, our hardware lead, and you'll get his answer as a reply in this thread.

So he can read it quickly, could you reply with:

1. The firmware name and version the dashboard shows. If it's Harlo OS, check harlolabs.com to see if a newer version is out, and if so update before anything else.
2. A screenshot of the two warnings, plus the hashrate and power the unit shows in normal mode once it has run for about 15 minutes.
3. Whether the two units came with identical power supplies. If they did, swap them between the miners, run both in normal mode, and tell me which unit shows the warnings afterwards. That tells us whether the problem is in the power supply or the miner.

If you'd like quicker hands-on help in the meantime, the Discord is very active: https://discord.gg/Q2R5sA9Fsf. Tag @nullhashrate, which is JD.

Hal, HeliumDeploy Technical Support

Handed to the team · Policy question I won't answer by guessing: is a Thor P2 that ships set to the m

Hi Cody,

You're right to push on this, and I didn't explain it well in my last email. Here's how it works.

Our warranty line is about the hashrate, not what the mode is called. The T. P2 is sold as a 10 TH/s miner, and our rule is that running it above 10 TH/s is what counts as overclocking. You're seeing 9.75 TH/s in the mode labelled overclock, which is under 10 TH/s. So you haven't gone past the line just by using the setting the unit came in. You're also right that this is in the FAQ part of the product page rather than the main description. It says 
this unit is rated at 10 TH/s. Running it above that, including any turbo or boost mode, is overclocking: it runs hotter, needs good airflow, and voids the warranty.
 The factory mode is set by the manufacturer, and I don't want to guess why they ship it that way. I've passed both questions to the team (does the mode it shipped in affect your warranty, and why is it the default) so you get a straight answer in this thread rather than mine.

On the second unit, I agree something is off. With both on the same model and the same firmware, one shouldn't run about 5°C hotter in normal mode than the other does in overclock. That usually comes down to one of three things: the power supply, airflow where it sits, or how well the heatsink is seated on the chips. Two quick tests will tell us which:

First, swap the power supplies between the two units, put them side by side with the same space around them, and run both in normal mode for about 15 minutes. Then raise the second unit's setting a little again and see whether the VBUS and powerboard warnings come back. If they follow the power supply, we know what's wrong.

Second, reply with a screenshot of each unit's dashboard showing hashrate, power, chip temperature, VR temperature (if it shows one) and fan speed, plus the firmware version. Please also confirm whether the "125" in your email is watts.

With those, JD (our hardware lead) can tell whether that unit needs anything. Until then, leave it in normal mode, which it runs fine in. If you'd like quicker hands-on help, the Discord is very active: https://discord.gg/Q2R5sA9Fsf. Tag @nullhashrate, which is JD.

Hal, HeliumDeploy Technical Support

Handed to the team · A part is needed and I have no store tools. JD, please confirm the nut's size/th

Hi Cody,

Good find, and thanks for the photo. It shows exactly what you described. At the end of the heatsink's metal retention bar there's a bare threaded post coming up through the hole with no nut on it, so that corner of the bracket isn't being held down. You're right that this shouldn't have left the factory that way.

It also explains everything you've seen on that unit. With one corner loose, the heatsink doesn't press evenly on the chips, so the unit runs hotter in normal mode than your other one does on a higher setting. Once you push it even slightly, the extra heat and load are the likely trigger for the VBUS and powerboard warnings. From what you've described and the photo, this looks like a missing part rather than a broken board.

To fix it yourself:

1. Unplug the miner first.
2. Check that the other bracket posts all have their nuts. Fit a matching nut on the bare post (a hardware store can match it if you take the unit or the post size with you).
3. Tighten it finger tight, then just a little more, so it's snug and matches the other corners. Don't crank it down, because too much pressure can crack a chip or bend the board.
4. Run it in normal mode for about 15 minutes and compare its temperature with the other unit. If it now runs about the same, try the small bump again and tell me whether the warnings come back.

If you'd rather not source the nut yourself, say so in your reply. I've passed the details to our hardware lead, JD, including confirming the exact nut size for this bracket. The team is offline now, picks this up tomorrow at 10am ET, and the answer will come to your email. If temperatures are still high after the nut is on, tell me before you touch the thermal paste so we can look at it together.

If you'd like help sooner, the Discord is active in the evenings: https://discord.gg/Q2R5sA9Fsf. Tag @nullhashrate, which is JD.

Hal, HeliumDeploy Technical Support
